setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Git and the current Node LTS are required.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

hints: If either line says "command not found", install it from the setup steps and then open a new terminal window — a just-installed tool is not on the PATH of a window that was already open.
cue needs Node 18 or newer. An older Node will clone and install and then fail to start.

steps.title: Copy cue to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d cue/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/cue.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A cue folder appears

hints: If Git says the destination path 'cue' already exists, you cloned it on an earlier attempt — carry on to the next step.
A 'could not resolve host' error is a network or proxy problem, not a problem with the address.

steps.title: Open the cue folder
steps.body: If it says no such file or directory, the clone step above didn't run — do that one first.
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the cue folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has git checkout succeeded — is there a detached-HEAD notice with a line beginning "HEAD is now at", rather than an error?

hints: The detached HEAD warning is expected. It means you are on the reviewed commit rather than on a branch.
If git says the pathspec did not match, the clone did not finish — run `git fetch --all` and try this line again.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.verifierLabel: The command finishes without an error

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has npm finished — has it printed its closing notices (funding, audit or vulnerability counts, npm warn/notice lines) and returned to a shell prompt waiting for the next command? Vulnerability counts and warnings are npm's normal output and do NOT mean this failed.

hints: The first install downloads Electron, which is large. A minute of no output is normal.
The vulnerability count and the `npm warn` lines are normal npm output, not a failure.
If npm reports the lockfile is out of sync with package.json, run `npm install` instead of `npm ci`.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.verifierLabel: dist/mac-arm64/cue.app exists

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has electron-builder finished — has it printed its build output (lines beginning with •, mentioning electron-builder, packaging or signing) and returned to a shell prompt waiting for the next command? Lines about skipped steps or a default icon are normal and do NOT mean this failed.

hints: The first build downloads electron-builder's own toolchain, so it can sit silent for a minute or two.
If npm says the script is missing, this window is not in the cue folder — `cd ~/cue` and run it again.

steps.title: Put cue in Applications
steps.body: Copy the freshly built app into Applications so it's a real, launchable Mac app.
steps.verifierLabel: cue.app is in your Applications folder

steps.title: Open cue
steps.body: Built on your own machine, so macOS opens it without any warning.
steps.verifierLabel: cue launches from its normal system shortcut

hints: cue has no Dock icon by design — it is the glass pill at the top of the screen. Click it once and Iris will see it.
If macOS asks for screen and microphone access again, that is expected: this is a different build from the one you ran with npm start.

steps.title: Allow screen and microphone access
steps.body: No cue row yet — switch on Iris (or Terminal, if you ran it) under Screen Recording and Microphone.
steps.verifierLabel: cue opens without a permission warning

steps.title: Add your own AI key
steps.body: Open Settings from the ••• button, pick a provider, paste the key.
steps.verifierLabel: cue answers a test question

hints: The ••• button is in cue's input box; ⌘, opens the same Settings panel.
Anthropic and OpenAI keys both work for screen and coding help, but only OpenAI or Gemini can transcribe a meeting.
